sittings.bodyEn: The same work is worth more in the buyer's mind when you split it into named parts and stack those parts as bonuses. Until you enumerate the parts, they stay invisible. Long-form ads set a price on one core item, then keep adding pieces until refusing feels hard to justify, and they keep the pattern because the minutes cost money. You widen the gap between price and value by adding value. Anchor the number you say to the core offer. Each added bonus stretches that gap, and this chapter is the order for revealing the stack you already built.

terms.hook: A named piece of the stack, with its own benefit, proof, and price tag.
The core price you state first, before extras widen the gap.

sittings.bodyEn: When a deal stalls, hold the price of the main offer. A discount teaches the buyer that the price was a suggestion and that pushing will be rewarded. Adding a bonus closes the deal from a position of strength and leaves goodwill where a concession would have left weakness. You will often deliver that piece anyway, and the timing of the reveal is what changes the perception. Tools, checklists, scripts, and templates beat another block of training as bonuses, because they cut effort and time, which raises value. Aim for a bonus stack whose tagged value can eclipse the core, so the core feels even more substantial beside it.

In a one-to-one sale, ask for the decision before you mention the bonuses. If they agree, reveal the extras after they have committed, so the surprise confirms the decision. If they decline, add one bonus aimed at the obstacle they just named, then ask again. Agree with the concern, add the piece, and ask whether the revised offer is fair. People struggle to refuse a concession built for the reason they just gave, and you can repeat the move with the next obstacle. Group presentations follow a different rhythm. This sequence is for one buyer in a conversation.

terms.hook: In a one-to-one sale, request the decision, then reveal or add a bonus from the answer.

sittings.bodyEn: Offer bonuses every time, drawing them from the bundle you kept after trimming. Put the benefit inside the bonus name so the title does the selling. Walk four facts in order: which fear it answers, what the piece actually is, the work it took to create, and the way their week gets faster or easier once they have it. Back the claim with a number, a client result, or a story from your own use. Describe a day after the bonus has done its job, so they can see the result as already real. Attach a price and the reason that price is fair. Reveal a single bonus at the moment it answers the doubt in front of you, and save the rest.

Each bonus should strike one reason the buyer believes they will fail, or solve the next problem before they reach it. As you add bonuses, the gap between price and value keeps widening. Buyers also assume the main thing must be worth more than the gifts, and that assumption makes the core feel larger. You can put a limit on the bonus itself. A scarcity version says these extras exist only inside the program, or that only a few event seats remain as bonuses. An urgency version says the extra is included if they buy today, as a reward for acting, and withheld if they wait. A count of seats and a same-day deadline are different limits, so say the one you will enforce.

Businesses that are direct competitors stay out, and neighboring businesses will contribute products or services in exchange for access to your customers. You receive extras you do not have to fulfill, and they receive exposure to people who already bought. A clinic might stack massages, adjustments, food discounts, support-gear savings, a training session, and pharmacy savings until those extras alone pass the price of the core. Ask several providers for the same kind of extra so the stack has depth. Negotiate a group rate the buyer could never get alone, because you represent many customers at once. If the partner pieces justify the price by themselves, the decision on the core gets easier.

terms.hook: A neighboring business supplies the extra, at a rate your buyer could not negotiate alone.

sittings.bodyEn: Ask the partner for a commission or a wholesale arrangement on the people you send. The bonus then does two jobs: more of your buyers say yes, and you are paid when they use the partner. A workable shape is a discount the customer cannot find on the public site, a share of that sale for the person who extended the discount, and a new customer for the supplier. Start with the next need your buyer will have after they begin with you, and go to that business first. Add the referral fees, and a modest core price can carry a second stream of profit on customers you already paid to acquire. You can build a full offer around the partner's piece so the bonus itself is a specific promise, rather than a generic coupon.

The best originals are checklists, tools, swipe files, scripts, and templates: costly to create, easy to use, and free to give again. Record every workshop, webinar, interview, and event, and pull one recording when it removes a specific fear. Information products fit this role because the perceived value is high, the cost is low, and delivery is another login. Tickets to a virtual event, or a short stretch of a higher service level, fit too, and the higher level can later become the upsell. Keep the set in a vault and add to it for as long as you operate. Use a few pieces to close a deal, and leave the rest for the next obstacle.

When you fulfill the piece yourself, pull it out as a bonus if the buyer would miss it inside a long list. Short, dense pieces qualify: a checklist or a one-page map that would feel too small to purchase alone and generous as a gift. The core remains the main transformation. Bonuses are the highlighted nuggets and the next problems along the path. Hold the core price while you do this. After the stack is presented, the objection still standing is risk, which a guarantee is built to remove. Reveal in this order: name the core price, add one bonus per fear, then reverse the risk.

Bonuses increase value while the core price stays put. Across the table from one buyer, request the decision while the extras are still unmentioned. A yes earns the extras as confirmation after they commit. A no earns one bonus matched to the stated obstacle, and then you ask again. Each bonus needs a benefit name, a link to their fear, proof, a picture of life after use, and a justified price. Tools that reduce effort beat another pile of lessons. The stack you trimmed is the inventory these bonuses come from.
sittings.prompt: When do you ask for the sale in a one-to-one conversation?
choices: Before you reveal bonuses, and add a matching bonus only if they decline
After you have read every bonus, discount, and guarantee out loud
Only after they request a lower price on the core offer
After you rename the offer, and leave the stack unspoken
